note: REGISTERED FORWARD TESTS. An admitted play merges PROVISIONAL and its test is recorded here against a NAMED group. The coordinator serves the DUE list into that group's run and hard-fails if a due test goes unreported.

tests.falsifier: If same-burn same-breadth November-vs-deep-winter week pairs stop differing by more than ~100 Bcf once weather-normal heating is accounted for - i.e. the gap turns out to be burn mismeasurement rather than the heating term - the size claim is wrong and A-38's converter build is mis-aimed. Also refuted if the A-38 weekly re-check on a full HDD join shows power burn matching heating's share of weekly variance in Dec-Feb.

Forward winter weeks with rising renewables AND heating-grade cold whose realized draws match the burn-implied size (no under-call) refute the masking claim. On the daily lane: forward days where a served renewables surge coexists with the weather-implied gas bump arriving in full refute the mediation form (0629/0601 class).

A forward cold+calm week delivering an ordinary draw with functioning price elasticity (no decoupling, no curtailment) refutes the flag's necessity at its stated strength. The hydro limb is separately falsifiable: a freeze event where hydro fails to rise above its month p50 WITHOUT drought conditions refutes the dispatch-buffer read - 2025-01-25..30 (593-642 vs p50 669) is the one recorded exception and rides with the play.

Refuted if a further year's cycle shows winter (Jan-Mar) p50 at or below late-summer (Jul-Aug) p50 absent drought; or if freeze events systematically show hydro FALLING below month p50 without drought (the 2025-01 exception becoming the rule); or if the drought winter, when it arrives, does NOT produce the outsized gas response the buffer framing implies.

A second summer week at breadth<=1 delivering a >=+100 Bcf build, or a summer draw arriving at breadth>=4, refutes the exclusion at its stated strength. The coverage falsifier: if adding the missing Southeast BAs (A-18) materially moves the breadth of past weeks, the count was a coverage artifact and must be re-measured before further use.

Forward shoulder days where large warm-removals (<= -1.0 GWDD) deliver DOWN days at ordinary base rates refute the shoulder inversion. Forward days where the census's largest revisions deliver the largest moves refute the size inversion. If high-disagreement days (>=0.7 GWDD spread) stop containing disproportionate outcome width, the authority channel claim falls.

A forward week landing beyond its month's listed seven-year extreme by more than ~15 Bcf refutes that month's gate at its stated strength - single-week, listable, cannot be missed. The anchor gates specifically: any February week shallower than -40, any May week below +45, any August week above +80, any October draw, any December build, any November week beyond ~+/-120. The hydro-asymmetry limb is refuted if a fall-shoulder freeze arrives and hydro cover proves irrelevant to the gas response.

If forward runs emit magnitudes above 550 on days whose drivers support it AND capture on |actual|>900 days does not improve above the measured 18-37% band, the ceiling was not the binding constraint and this play is wrong. Equally refuted if raising emissions degrades sum|err| - i.e. if the cap was doing useful work - which would mean the honest bar is correctly calibrated and the loss is elsewhere.

If specialists run under the seven-step order and (a) no posterior shows a pre-influence read differing from its post-chain estimate, or (b) emissions still cap at ~550 where drivers support more, or (c) no override is ever declined for lacking an independent read, then the order changed no behaviour and is ceremony. Refuted also if ordering the steps DEGRADES sum|err| against the s105.3 baseline.

tests.hypothesis: Greg, S114: 'That will probably help clear up our unattached days and part of the drift.' The mission brief tells a specialist the path is ONE continuous object sampled at eight times, that each point inherits from the one before, and that its day is a link in a chain rather than a standalone estimate. If the unattached-day and drift problems are partly an ORIENTATION fault - agents told to do math and never told the values flow together - the brief should move them.
tests.what_is_measured_and_it_does_not_need_th: These are SHAPE properties, measurable on a contaminated rehearsal as well as a fresh run, which matters because g22/g23 have already seen the curve (D39: we test ON the runs, not against them). (a) ATTACHMENT: day N's emitted close level vs day N+1's emitted open level - the count of days that do not connect. (b) CONTRACT ARITHMETIC: first path point == 0 and last == (day-move minus gap); S110 measured g23 at 8 of 10 days mismatched, both Mondays by exactly +400. (c) STEP STRUCTURE: path segments that move with no named liquidity event between them. (d) DRIFT SHARE: |drift| as a fraction of sum|err| - the 'survives' number, which is the part of the error that does NOT cancel and is therefore the part a continuity fault would produce.
tests.falsifier: REFUTED if, under the brief, (a) the unattached-day count and the contract-arithmetic mismatch count are no better than the s105.5 baseline, AND (b) drift share is unchanged or worse. Refuted independently if specialists report the brief but their posteriors show no reference to inheritance between points - i.e. it was read and not used. NOTE THE ASYMMETRY: a fall in drift share alone does NOT confirm it, because drift share also falls when the market gets quieter - that exact artifact produced the fake 939 -> 592 'improvement' (realized moves fell 799 -> 457 over the same span). Confirmation requires the mechanical counts (a) to move.
tests.baseline_named_per_A1: s105.5 blind, same block. g22 blind of record: 4/10 direction, sum|err| 5,965, drift -1,815, survives 30%. The mechanical counts (attachment, contract arithmetic) must be computed on that committed blind BEFORE the rehearsal, or there is no baseline to beat.
